page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native server family instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and utilizes a shared resource allocation model. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks show a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is rated in the bottom 10% with a score of 784.69, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and modest 2.0 GHz clock speed. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 9386.85 and a PassMark CPU score of 22472.2. Memory bandwidth is stable, measuring 1218.59 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 60.68 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

This instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage the 12 vCPUs, such as static web serving, which achieves a throughput of 9.63 GB/sec, and Redis operations, which reach 17.86 million SET operations per second. It also supports light LLM inference, processing 1083.04 tokens per second for a small 135M model, though text generation for a medium 7B model drops to a poor 6.21 tokens per second. Qualitatively, the shared CPU model offers a cost-effective entry point for multi-core processing where sustained peak single-core performance is not critical.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native virtual server utilizing the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor, it offers 12 shared vCPUs and 12 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 24.0 GB of RAM. This configuration yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with no local storage bundled. Benchmark data indicates a trade-off: single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance and memory bandwidth reach average tiers, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 22472.2. The instance is well-suited for multi-threaded, budget-conscious workloads such as static web serving, Redis database operations, and basic multi-threaded decompression, where shared CPU resources provide a cost-effective alternative to dedicated cores.
